physics_goals.quote: measuring with unprecedented sensitivity the spectrum, composition, and anisotropy of cosmic rays in the energy range between 10^12 and 10^18 eV, and acting simultaneously as a wide aperture (one stereoradiant) continuously operating gamma-ray telescope in the energy range between 10^11 and 10^15 eV
physics_goals.value: Measure the cosmic-ray energy spectrum, composition and anisotropy from 10^12 to 10^18 eV, and survey the sky as a wide-aperture gamma-ray telescope with sensitivity to PeV-scale ('PeVatron') sources.

summary.plain: A high-altitude Chinese observatory that measures cosmic rays and hunts for the highest-energy gamma rays in the sky, using several kinds of detectors together on a mountain 4410 metres up.
summary.technical: Multi-component air-shower observatory at 4410 m on Haizi Mountain, Sichuan, China, combining water-Cherenkov, muon/electromagnetic and Cherenkov-telescope sub-arrays (per public description; individual KM2A/WCDA/WFCTA specifications not sourced this session) to cover cosmic-ray energies of 10^12-10^18 eV and gamma rays above 100 TeV. Reported as already operating by May 2021, with UHE photons up to 1.4 PeV detected from twelve Galactic sources.

unique_capabilities.quote: detected ultra-high-energy (UHE; E_gamma >~ 100 TeV) photon emissions up to 1.4 PeV from twelve astrophysical gamma-ray sources
unique_capabilities.value: Detected ultra-high-energy photons up to 1.4 PeV from twelve Galactic gamma-ray sources, the highest-energy photons observed from astrophysical sources at the time of that 2021 report.
